title: Constructing number systems: integers, rationals, and real numbers

based_on.title: Set Theory: An Open Introduction
based_on.pages: 73–88 (§§6.1–6.6, quotient constructions and Dedekind cuts; online revision July 2026)

summary: Quotients supply integers and rationals; cuts fill rational gaps to give the complete real field.
abstract: Extending the natural numbers lets subtraction produce integers and division by nonzero numbers produce rationals, while preserving the arithmetic already available. Yet the rational number line still has gaps. Real numbers fill these gaps so that every nonempty collection bounded above has a smallest upper bound. All these number systems can be constructed from sets, and the resulting complete ordered field is unique up to a matching that preserves arithmetic and order.
